*Weekly Sector Rotation Report* | Week Ending ~Jun 21, 2026

---

*🔼 SECTORS ROTATING IN (5d vs SPY)*

- *Technology (+3.0% vs SPY)* — AI chip narrative dominant; MU earnings anticipation and Trump chip alliance signals driving semis (Reuters: "Micron earnings as pulse check of AI rally"; Benzinga: US chip alliance); MTUM +6.2% 5d confirms momentum concentration here
- *Industrials (+1.8% vs SPY)* — Broad risk-on rotation plus defense adjacent flows; XLI flat on the week but outperforming on risk-adjusted basis vs defensive peers
- *Utilities (+0.1% vs SPY)* — Mild relative outperformance vs staples/REIT; likely rate-sensitivity bid as TLT +0.9% 5d signals modest bond rally despite hawkish Warsh framing (CNBC: "AI buildout gives tech investors new reasons to watch bond market")

---

*🔽 SECTORS ROTATING OUT (5d vs SPY)*

- *Energy (-7.3% vs SPY)* — U.S.-Iran peace talks remove geopolitical risk premium; Strait of Hormuz de-escalation weighing on crude (CNBC/Reuters); SU, EOG, APA, PBR all negative
- *Healthcare (-4.5% vs SPY)* — Sector-wide pressure; UHS -15.5% from cost basis a notable drag, likely earnings/guidance specific; PODD -5.8% adds med-device weight
- *Comm. Services (-3.9% vs SPY)* — No specific catalyst; likely rotation out of defensive/ad-spend sensitive names; PINS -1.6% consistent with this

---

*📐 FACTOR ROTATION*

- *Momentum vs. Defensive:* MTUM +6.2% 5d vs USMV -1.2% — sharpest factor divergence this week; market clearly rewarding high-beta/momentum expression
- *Growth over Value:* Tech/semis leading, XLP -2.3% 5d; Value Picks portfolio is the worst-performing cluster
- *Macro framing:* TLT +0.9% and UUP +1.3% both positive — unusual co-move. Suggests Warsh hawkishness is lifting USD while short-end fear bids long bonds. Not a clean risk-on signal; watch for duration squeeze if rate hike expectations firm further (CNBC: "Markets set for more hawkish Warsh Fed")

---

*📁 PORTFOLIO P&L READS*

- *AI Defense & Autonomous:* Broad sector underperformance — defense names off 2-6%; no headline catalyst to reverse. GD (+1.2%) the lone hold. Likely Iran peace talks removing geopolitical bid (Reuters/CNBC Hormuz)
- *Growth Value:* Mixed but net positive — SEZL +7.5%, BOOT +3.6%, NBIX +3.3% offsetting HMY/BZ drags. Fintech/consumer discretionary names catching momentum bid
- *Income Dividends:* Energy names (SU, EOG) and SCCO (-3.7%) dragging; portfolio functionally short the two worst rotating sectors this week
- *Innovation Fund:* Z (-21.3% from cost) is the dominant P&L event — likely earnings miss or guidance cut; needs monitoring. CAI +14.2% and RDDT/SHOP +3.4% partially offset
- *Momentum Growth:* Best-performing portfolio directionally — semis (MU, AMAT, WDC), TER all positive; aligned with MTUM factor move
- *Value Picks:* Significant stress — UHS -15.5%, BVN -11.1%, HRB -10.8%; multiple single-name events compounding sector headwinds
- *Nuclear Renaissance:* Flat-to-slightly negative; utilities rotating in at sector level but nuclear-specific names not catching the bid meaningfully; CCJ -1.6%

---

*🚩 POSITIONS TO FLAG*

1. *Z (Innovation Fund, -21.3%)* — Magnitude of drawdown from cost suggests a discrete negative event (earnings/guidance). Warrants review of thesis vs. current price action; XLRE -2.4% 5d confirms real estate tech headwinds
2. *UHS (Value Picks, -15.5%)* — Healthcare sector weakest vs SPY (-4.5% 5d); company-specific move this large within a down sector suggests potential guidance cut or legal/regulatory item; thesis validation needed
3. *MU/WDC (Momentum Growth)* — Benzinga flags DRAM ETF risk reversal risk and MU earnings as market "pulse check" (Reuters); both up 5d but positioned at a binary event — magnitude of AI trade concentration warrants close attention into earnings

---

*👀 DIVERGENCES WORTH WATCHING*

1. *TLT + UUP both bid simultaneously* — Hawkish Warsh repricing is unusual; if the market begins pricing a 2026 hike (CNBC: "several members signal a hike"), both growth and income portfolios face duration/valuation headwinds that current 5d returns don't yet reflect
2. *Defense underperforming despite geopolitical noise* — Iran-U.S. talks are reducing the risk premium that likely underpinned this portfolio's entry thesis; worth watching whether GD's relative strength is a sector tell or an outlier
